title: SAC Sends 1,000+ Reinforcements Including Tanks Into Shwegu Township — KIA Battles Back as Kachin Frontier Escalates
detail: Myanmar's military junta dispatched more than 1,000 reinforcements — including armored vehicles and tanks — into Shwegu Township, Kachin State (on the Kachin-Sagaing border), triggering fierce fighting with Kachin Independence Army (KIA) forces from May 2, 2026. The deployment of armor into Shwegu represents a significant escalation of junta operations in eastern Kachin State, a region where the KIA has been expanding its offensive reach throughout 2026. Shwegu is strategically important as it sits on the Irrawaddy River corridor connecting Kachin State to northern Sagaing Region — the same axis where KIA-led forces were pressing toward Indaw on the Katha axis as of April 29. The junta's armored reinforcement into Shwegu appears designed to cut KIA supply lines and prevent the connection of KIA operations in northern Kachin (Hpakant, Putao, Myitkyina) with KIA-allied forces advancing in northern Sagaing. MoeMaKa CDM News documented the reinforcement dispatch in its May 4, 2026 report, noting the battles remained intense throughout the May 2-4 period.

media.caption: SAC sends 1,000+ reinforcements including tanks into Shwegu Township (Kachin State) — KIA fights back as junta attempts to cut KIA operational corridor to northern Sagaing, May 2, 2026

title: SAC Airstrike Campaign Kills 10+ Children Under Age 12 in Myingyan and Taungtha Townships — Incendiary Bombs, Drones, Gyrocopters, and Artillery Used
detail: A Mizzima English investigation published May 2, 2026 documented that more than 10 children under age 12 were killed in a single week (approximately April 20–27) in Myingyan and Taungtha townships in central Myanmar through a sustained SAC aerial and artillery campaign. Weapons documented included incendiary bombs dropped by jet fighters, armed drones, gyrocopters, paramotors, and howitzer shelling by Light Infantry Battalion 15. On April 22, strikes on Yon Htoe village destroyed a monastery and surrounding homes. The junta's 'scorched earth' policy in the area reportedly escalated following recent changes in local military administration leadership. A 12-year-old girl was also killed by SAC artillery fire in Moe Tain Pyin Village, Natogyi Township, in the same period. Separately, Mizzima reported 11 civilians killed in the Kyin Dway Bridge double-tap strike in Kanpetlet Township (Chin State) from the same period. The killing of 10+ children in one week represents one of the most intensive child-targeting patterns documented by Mizzima in 2026, consistent with a deliberate SAC policy of collective punishment in areas with resistance presence. The use of incendiary weapons against civilian areas violates customary international humanitarian law.

media.caption: SAC incendiary bombs, drones, gyrocopters, and artillery kill 10+ children under age 12 in Myingyan and Taungtha townships (central Myanmar) in one week; Mizzima investigation published May 2, 2026
